description:
AstroCultureX — From Space to Soil

We are passionate about space technology, web development, AI, and sustainable agriculture. Our NASA Space Apps 2026 project, FieldShift, explores how NASA data can help farmers improve crop rotation, soil health, water use, and climate resilience.

We welcome developers, designers, data enthusiasts, and agriculture lovers, including beginners. Join us to turn space science into practical solutions for farmers!
summary:
Furrow Fields (“From space to soil”) is a web app that turns NASA Earth-observation data into plain-language farming decisions for any field on Earth. A farmer pins a location and sees 30 years of NASA POWER temperature, rainfall and root-zone soil wetness, NASA GIBS plant-health and rainfall layers, and a European ERA5 and Sentinel-2 cross-check. Future Weather gives a 2-month outlook and a 15-year Climate Twin on a 3D globe. Both are calculated from NASA data, not guessed by AI. Crop Plan and Best Crops rank 26 crops using FAO EcoCrop thresholds. Gemini AI only explains results and translates. The site works in 43 languages plus 100+ language codes, and the Ask Sprout assistant answers in any language. Farmer Talk lets farmers around the world connect and share advice.

It matters because smallholder farmers often plant on guesswork. Scientific data is hard for them to use and rarely in their language. Furrow Fields makes that data usable and checkable for them
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

Furrow Fields (From space to soil) is a global smart-farming web app, and also a Progressive Web App (PWA), that turns satellite climate data and agricultural science into clear guidance for any field on Earth. Users start on a Landing Page that explains the features, how to use the site and how the data is verified, then click Dashboard. They search a city or village, click the map, or tap Use my location. The app sends the coordinates to a FastAPI backend, which retrieves NASA POWER monthly climate and root-zone soil moisture data, scores 26 major crops against FAO EcoCrop thresholds, generates the top 3 multi-season crop rotations, computes a 2-month weather outlook, and matches the field to a 3D Climate Twin across 220 global farming regions. Users explore five tabs (My Field, Future Weather, Crop Plan, Best Crops, Farmer Talk) plus Ask Sprout, an AI agronomist, and a Universal Language Switcher.

2. What benefits does it have?

Science-backed decisions anywhere: it works for any coordinate on Earth with no local weather station. No language barrier: the whole interface is translated into 43 named languages and 100+ ISO language codes, with automatic right-to-left layout for Urdu, Arabic, Persian, Pashto and Sindhi, and Ask Sprout chats in any language the farmer types. Independent verification: NASA POWER data is cross-checked against Open-Meteo ERA5 Reanalysis and Sentinel-2 L2A imagery. Fast, free and browser-based: as a PWA it works on desktop and mobile and can be installed like an app, using 6-hour server caching and browser caching for translations.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

To empower smallholder farmers, agronomists and rural communities worldwide, especially in non-English-speaking and climate-vulnerable regions. Farmers can replace planting guesswork with data-driven crop and rotation planning, anticipate dry or wet windows and long-term climate shifts early, and connect with other farmers on Farmer Talk (Chaupal) to share local observations across language barriers.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Languages: Python (backend), HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript (frontend), built as a Progressive Web App (PWA). Backend: FastAPI, Uvicorn, httpx, cachetools. Mapping and 3D: Leaflet.js, Three.js / WebGL 3D globe, Esri ArcGIS World Imagery and Labels, OpenStreetMap, and NASA GIBS WMTS (MODIS_Terra_NDVI_8Day, IMERG_Precipitation_Rate). Data: NASA POWER API (T2M, PRECTOTCORR, GWETROOT), FAO EcoCrop database, Open-Meteo ERA5 Reanalysis, Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC (Sentinel-2 L2A) and geocoding APIs. AI, translation and community: Google Gemini API (gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-2.5-flash), Google Translate GTX fallback, Firebase Anonymous Authentication and Cloud Firestore. Development and hosting: Git and GitHub, Vercel (frontend) and Render (backend). No special hardware was used.

5. How is your project creative?

Interactive 3D Climate Twin globe: instead of climate tables, it draws a 3D arc on Earth from a farmer's field today to a real farming region that matches the field's projected climate 15 years from now. Grounded AI: Ask Sprout only reasons over the pinned field's live NASA and FAO data and replies in the farmer's own language, instead of giving generic chatbot answers. Borderless multilingual design: instant right-to-left and left-to-right layout switching, typo-tolerant search across 100+ languages, and a live translated farmer forum (Chaupal) in one platform.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Accessibility and language equity: farmers speak many languages, so we built right-to-left support, quick English/Urdu switching, 100+ ISO code support and mobile-friendly navigation. Scientific accuracy and transparency: AI never invents weather or crop numbers. All scores come from NASA POWER and FAO EcoCrop, with rule-based fallbacks if AI quota is unavailable. Performance and reliability: 6-hour caching for NASA POWER and ERA5 queries, 10-second request timeouts with retries, and browser caching for translations. Security and privacy: the Gemini API key stays on the server, and Firebase Anonymous Auth lets farmers join discussions without a complicated sign-up.
